I love this game. The content is always expanding. Of course that means regular updates which can get annoying. Between the leveling chart, skill gems, and randomized weapon enhancements, it has fantastic customizing options for characters.

The UI is a little jank but there's tons of quality ARPG meat to bite into here. I suspect I'll be doing several playthroughs as I learn the systems. You make semi-permanent choices along the way so first time play is going to be naive while creating your first build. Not as purely polished as that which shall not be named but it's the better, superior successor to everyone's favorite demonic ARPG. Microtransactions are not annoying, nor necessary and only slightly manipulative (stash tabs which you will want). Very reasonable approach.

I own Diablo, Diablo 2, Diablo 3, Torchlight 2, Path of Exile, Titan Quest, and various other action RPG's in this genre.

Diablo 2 is the older,superior game that all other games are compared to in the genre. That being said, I find Path of Exile to be the worthy successor to Diablo 2.

Contrasting it to similar titles, Path of Exile offers a complex yet rewarding experience. It trumps others with its deep mechanics and extensive customization. However, its steep learning curve may deter casual players.

Path of Exile is the quintessential ARPG. It has a challenge that keeps on giving, a dark and gripping atmosphere, deep and compelling sotry, comprehensive and vast character customization, quality music, and much much more.

Grinding Gear Games has not only created a masterpiece, but also continues to do what few developers refuse to: listen to their fans and morph the already fantastic game to make it even better. Every time a patch comes around, it's something people have been asking for, and there's not a single time I've looked at patch notes and not gotten excited.

I would recommend this game to anyone - fans of the genre or not.

Think of the elements that made Diablo II great, meddle it with Torchlight and add some new stuff: the result is Path of Exile, a game that is far too good to be a free to play game. You don't even need to play anything to become superior to the other players: the microtransactions are moslty cosmetics. There are paid games out there that don't have 10% of PoE's quality. Everything in this game is perfect; only the story is a little confusing and uninspiring, but the lore is pleasant. From the reliable community to the constant patches, this is a very friendly game, both for you and for your low-end PC. Without prolonging this review a lot more, let me just say that it took me about 20 hours to do a single playthough, which is a lot more than some AAA titles present. If you like ARPG, or just RPG, or even just a action game, there is no excuse for not to, at least, try this wonderful game. I give it a 92 out of 100. Best free to play game of 2013 and probably one of the best free to play games out there.

Currently in my first League (Affliction) and the game is fantastic. The amount of ground to cover and real sense of progression is apparent throughout the whole experience. I wouldn't recommend trying to learn the game mechanics and class progression by yourself for the first experience, a guide will go a long way in teaching you the basics without having to worry too much about your character. This is not a very casual friendly ARPG as overall the game has a very steep learning curve which will have you bouncing in between video guide content and POE wiki content frequently. Very fun if you are willing to invest time and learning, also the amount of content is insane. There are games within games here especially when you get to endgame mapping. 9/10. -1 for the one shot mechanics that are inevitable.

Path of Exile is an exceptionally well-crafted ARPG that stands in a class of its own among ARPGs I've recently played. Its unique draw is the ability for you to "shape" your own endgame by choosing the type of content you wish to engage with upon reaching the late-game stage (after act 10). This level of flexibility is rare and greatly enhances the game's appeal.

However, there are two caveats to consider:
a) The game requires a high-performance computer for the best experience. Even with my fairly powerful setup equipped with a 3070ti, I've occasionally run into stutter lags when battling more than 50 enemies at once on-screen.
b) You may find yourself somewhat pressured to purchase stash tabs through the Microtransaction market, as the in-game trading system is tied to "public" stash tabs.

Despite these points, I wholeheartedly recommend Path of Exile. The game itself is free to play, and I view the one-time purchase of stash tabs as a fair form of monetization.

Probably not the best ARPG to start with, but insanely fun and beautiful, when you aren't dying every second that is. I tried playing it casually for most of the acts. I did well, but soon, I realized how badly I was being penalized for not finding a build and sticking to it. Near the end, it just felt like I was throwing myself at bosses until they died and I literally did. One of the things I do look forward in a game is a good story, and I was taken away as to how well Path of Exile worldbuilded. I probably had some bias at first since it's technically a free game. Despite my frustrations with the learning curves and difficulty scales, I enjoyed playing this game and even bought micro transactions (storage space since I kept running out). Shortly, great game but not the best for casual players who aren't willing to learn.

Probably the most in depth and replayable ARPG at the moment. There are over a hundred skills I believe, and two massive skill trees to work with. Also over 100 mid-end game maps, and a lot of modifiers you can add with scarabs. Every 3-4 months starts a new league with fresh mechanics. So again more replayablility. 
The game is all about zooming and kill kill kill, without many quests or much of a story. It does have those, but they aren't the focus. So if you're looking for a story rich roleplaying game, this isn't it.
The game is free unless you really get into it, then you will want stash tabs, but they go on sale often and reasonably priced.
Only thing that irks me is the losing level progression on death, but truly it's only an issue post level 95. And you can always slow down and play it safe.

An excellent alternative to more casual multiplayer ARPGs such as Diablo. The complex economy and class systems will be a huge turn off if you aren't ready to invest many hours into learning the game, but once you break through that barrier Path of Exile has almost endless re-playability. Especially with the leagues that are added every few months or so.

You don't have to pay a cent to get started in this game, however you will find that certain things like Stash Tabs are a necessity to playing long term. If you like this game, be prepared to drop some cash on it.

As with most ARPGs of this type, multiplayer doesn't really feel good in my opinion. Because you can quickly out-level your friends, playing through the same content together requires a lot of coordination and will inevitably slow your progress. End-game maps and boss runs are an exception. If you play this with friends, most likely you'll just be talking about it together and playing at the same time... rather than actually "playing together".

I have over 1600 hours in the game. Probably more because that's just the hours I have through steam. Now, that's nothing compared to some of the dedicated streamers, but compared to the average player it's an insane amount of time.

Furthermore I've literally only ever quit one game because it doesn't respect the Player's time enough and that game was Lost Ark. So when I say that the recent changes and the indication for the sort of changes that are coming with 3.20 have managed to put this game on a path to respecting your time *less* than Lost Ark, maybe that's your cue to go check out Last Epoch, Undecember, Torchlight, or literally any other ARPG other than this one. Personally, I've been putting time into Last Epoch when I need to itch the ARPG scratch. That used to be PoE. It will no longer be PoE and without serious changes in the mindset from the devs, I'll probably never touch this game again.

I wouldn't say completely don't play this game, as there's still *some* fun left in it, if you're a new player. But I would say don't spend a single fucking penny on this game and also you need to expect that it's going to require unreasonable time investments for your builds to come to fruition.

As a big fan of Diablo 2's visual presentation coupled with great music and a broody, dark and menacing atmosphere I found myself very dissappointed with Diablo 3. That said I was very relieved when I first played the beta to Path of Exile. Although the beta for POE was not as polished and the gameplay abit clunky compared to D3, when POE launched the final version they did so with "guns ablazing". The final version is slick, fluid and visually pleasing. And with the FF7 inspired "MATERIA" or "GEMS" as POE calls them I find no reason to return to the D3 debauchery that many of us waited so long for. In the end I give POE an 8\10 only falling short a 9\10 because of how short the game is. But I highly recommend POE to anyone who is a fan of action RPG's and Diablo 2.
